dockerfile_copy_all.benefit: Smaller image, no accidental secret exposure in container layers.

dockerfile_unpinned_base.benefit: Reproducible builds, protection against supply chain attacks.

eval_injection_php.benefit: Prevention of remote code running (OWASP A03, CWE-94).

cookie_broad_path.title: Cookie path too broad

cookie_broad_path.benefit: Limits cookie scope to the minimum required path, reducing exposure surface.

db_superuser_connection_csharp.risk: A database connection string uses a privileged account (sa, root, admin, postgres). db_superuser_connection_csharp.benefit: Limits blast radius of a compromised application — an attacker can only access what the dedicated user is allowed to.

dont_install_root_cert.title: Certificate added to the root store
dont_install_root_cert.risk: Adding a certificate to the system root certificate store (StoreName.Root) makes it trusted for all processes on the machine — an attacker who gains code execution can install a certificate for a malicious CA, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks against any HTTPS connection on the system (CWE-327).

Use StoreName.My (personal store) for application-specific certificates. Never add certificates to StoreName.Root. If a custom CA is required, add it to StoreName.CertificateAuthority with a minimal scope.

dont_install_root_cert.benefit: Prevents weakening of system-wide TLS trust by adding application-specific certificates to the root store.

ecb_mode_csharp.title: ECB encryption mode (C#)
ecb_mode_csharp.risk: Electronic Codebook (ECB) mode encrypts each block independently with the same key — identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks, revealing data patterns and making it possible to detect repetitions and correlate encrypted blocks without decrypting them (CWE-327).

ecb_mode_csharp.benefit: Prevents data pattern leakage via ECB mode deterministic encryption.

exposure_private_information.title: Private information in API responses

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Project only the fields the client legitimately needs using a DTO or anonymous type. Apply [JsonIgnore] to sensitive properties on model classes. Implement field-level authorization to exclude sensitive fields based on the caller's role.

exposure_private_information.benefit: Prevents excessive data exposure of private user information in API responses.

exposure_transmitted_data.benefit: Prevents accidental exposure of sensitive data in API responses.

local_unvalidated_arithmetic.benefit: Prevents buffer overflow via unvalidated pointer arithmetic in unsafe code.

unmanaged_resource_leak_on_error.title: Unmanaged resource leaked on error
unmanaged_resource_leak_on_error.risk: A stream/bitmap/unmanaged handle is allocated without a using block or explicit Dispose(). If parsing fails partway through (malformed input, invalid header/geometry), the handle is never released — an attacker who controls the input can repeatedly trigger the leak and exhaust memory or file handles (CWE-401), as seen in several image/document decoder CVEs.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Wrap the allocation in a using statement (or using var) so the resource is released even when an exception is thrown during parsing.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unmanaged_resource_leak_on_error.benefit: Guarantees deterministic release of native/unmanaged resources even on malformed or malicious input, preventing memory-exhaustion denial of service.

unsafe_deserialization_delegate.title: BinaryFormatter or SoapFormatter deserialization
unsafe_deserialization_delegate.risk: BinaryFormatter and SoapFormatter can deserialize arbitrary .NET types including delegates and code-execution gadget chains — an attacker who controls the serialized data can execute arbitrary code during deserialization, even from seemingly benign inputs (CWE-502).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Replace BinaryFormatter/SoapFormatter with a safe serializer. For JSON use System.Text.Json or Newtonsoft.Json with TypeNameHandling.None. For binary use MessagePack or Protobuf with typed message classes (no polymorphic deserialization).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_deserialization_delegate.benefit: Prevents arbitrary code execution via malicious serialized .NET objects.

use_after_dispose.title: Object used after Dispose()
use_after_dispose.risk: An object's Dispose() is called on an error/cleanup path, but the same variable is still used afterwards in the same scope. If Dispose() has already released the underlying native handle or unmanaged memory (as it does for streams, GDI+ objects, and P/Invoke wrappers), the later use operates on freed memory — Use After Free (CWE-416), which can crash the process or, in unmanaged interop, be exploited for memory corruption.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Ensure Dispose() is the last operation on an object (ideally via a using statement), and never reference the variable again afterwards in the same code path.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

use_after_dispose.benefit: Eliminates use-after-free crashes and potential memory-corruption issues caused by continued use of a disposed object.

xml_injection_csharp.title: XML injection (C#)
xml_injection_csharp.risk: Constructing or parsing XML with user-controlled content without proper escaping allows XML injection — an attacker can break out of the intended XML structure, inject additional elements or attributes, or corrupt the document schema (CWE-091).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use SecurityElement.Escape() or XmlConvert.EncodeName() to escape user values before embedding in XML. Better yet, use the XML API to build documents programmatically (XElement, XmlDocument) rather than string concatenation.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xml_injection_csharp.benefit: Prevents XML injection attacks via user-controlled XML content.

xxe_xmldocument.title: XXE through XmlDocument
xxe_xmldocument.risk: Using XmlDocument with a non-null XmlResolver (the default in older .NET versions) is vulnerable to XXE (XML External Entity) — an attacker can include external entity references in XML that cause the parser to read local files (/etc/passwd, web.config) or make SSRF requests to internal services (CWE-611).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Set XmlResolver = null on XmlDocument before loading any content: var doc = new XmlDocument { XmlResolver = null }; In .NET 4.5.2+ the default XmlResolver is null for XmlDocument, but explicitly setting it is recommended for clarity.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xxe_xmldocument.benefit: Prevents XXE attacks via external entity resolution in XmlDocument.

zip_slip_csharp.title: Zip Slip (C#)
zip_slip_csharp.risk: Using ZipArchiveEntry.FullName directly as a file path for extraction allows Zip Slip attacks — a malicious archive can contain entries with paths like "../../../etc/cron.d/backdoor" or "..\\..\\Windows\\System32\\malicious.dll" that extract files outside the target directory (CWE-022).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Combine the destination directory with the entry name using Path.GetFullPath(), then verify the result starts with the destination directory path followed by a directory separator.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

zip_slip_csharp.benefit: Prevents path traversal attacks via malicious archive entry names.

data_uri_html_tag.title: Data URI HTML in tag
data_uri_html_tag.risk: src/href with data:text/html loads executable HTML content directly in the browser (CWE-79).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Forbid data:text/html in src and href attributes.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

data_uri_html_tag.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

dom_clobbering.title: DOM Clobbering
dom_clobbering.risk: Elements named 'location', 'document', etc. override global JavaScript properties, enabling XSS or logic bypass (CWE-79).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Avoid using JavaScript global property names as HTML element id or name attributes.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

dom_clobbering.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

inline_event_handler_html.title: Inline event handler in HTML
inline_event_handler_html.risk: on* attributes in HTML execute JavaScript directly, vulnerable to XSS (CWE-79).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Move JavaScript to separate .js files with addEventListener().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

inline_event_handler_html.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

javascript_uri_html.title: javascript: URI in HTML attribute
javascript_uri_html.risk: href/action/src with javascript: executes arbitrary code on click or load (CWE-79).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use normal URIs (/, #, https://) and event handlers.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

javascript_uri_html.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

arithmetic_extreme_values.title: Arithmetic on extreme integer values
arithmetic_extreme_values.risk: Arithmetic on Integer.MAX_VALUE or Integer.MIN_VALUE overflows silently — MAX_VALUE + 1 wraps to MIN_VALUE and MIN_VALUE - 1 wraps to MAX_VALUE. If the result is used as an index, size, or security-sensitive quantity, the wrap-around produces an incorrect value (CWE-190, CWE-191).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use Math.addExact/subtractExact/multiplyExact to throw ArithmeticException on overflow. Alternatively, widen to long before arithmetic, or use BigInteger for safety.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

arithmetic_extreme_values.benefit: Prevents silent integer overflow when using boundary values in arithmetic.

arithmetic_tainted.title: Arithmetic on unvalidated user input
arithmetic_tainted.risk: Using user-supplied numeric values in arithmetic operations without bounds validation can lead to integer overflow or underflow — if the result is used as an array index, buffer size, or financial calculation, overflow can cause out-of-bounds access, heap corruption, or incorrect financial computations (CWE-190, CWE-191).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Validate user-supplied integers against expected ranges before use: if (value < MIN || value > MAX) throw new IllegalArgumentException(). Use Math.addExact/multiplyExact to detect overflow in arithmetic operations.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

arithmetic_tainted.benefit: Prevents integer overflow attacks leading to out-of-bounds access or incorrect calculations.

arithmetic_uncontrolled.title: Arithmetic on unvalidated configuration values
arithmetic_uncontrolled.risk: Arithmetic operations on values read from configuration files, system properties, or environment variables without bounds validation can cause integer overflow or underflow — if the result is used as a buffer size, array index, or financial amount, the overflow leads to unexpected behavior, memory corruption, or incorrect calculations (CWE-190, CWE-191).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate configuration-derived values against expected ranges before arithmetic. Use Math.addExact/multiplyExact to detect overflow. Add Javadoc documenting the expected value range.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

arithmetic_uncontrolled.benefit: Prevents integer overflow from unvalidated configuration values used in arithmetic.

array_construction_tainted.title: Array sized by user input
array_construction_tainted.risk: Creating an array with a size derived from user input without upper-bound validation allows an attacker to force allocation of arbitrarily large arrays — a request with size=2147483647 causes OutOfMemoryError or triggers heap exhaustion denial of service. Negative values cause NegativeArraySizeException (CWE-129, CWE-190).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate the size is within a safe range [0, MAX] before allocating: int size = Integer.parseInt(request.getParameter("n")); if (size < 0 || size > MAX_SIZE) throw new IllegalArgumentException().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

array_construction_tainted.benefit: Prevents denial-of-service via user-controlled array size allocation.

array_index_validation.title: Unvalidated array index from user input
array_index_validation.risk: Using a user-supplied value directly as an array index without validation allows out-of-bounds access — an attacker providing a negative value or a value larger than the array length can cause ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (DoS) or, in native/unsafe code, memory corruption (CWE-129, CWE-190).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate the index is within range [0, array.length) before use. Throw an appropriate exception for out-of-range values.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

array_index_validation.benefit: Prevents out-of-bounds array access via user-controlled index values.

auth_check_fail_open_on_exception.title: Authentication check fails open on exception
auth_check_fail_open_on_exception.risk: When the authentication/token-verification call throws, the catch block lets the request continue through the filter chain instead of denying it. Any error during auth verification (a malformed token, a downstream Keycloak/IdP outage, an unexpected exception) causes the security check to fail open — CWE-287, Improper Authentication.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
On any exception during authentication, deny the request explicitly (return 401/403) instead of letting it proceed. Never treat "verification failed" the same as "verification not required".
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

auth_check_fail_open_on_exception.benefit: Ensures authentication failures — including infrastructure errors — always result in access being denied (fail closed), not silently granted.

authz_bypass_raw_uri_check.title: Access check on the raw request URI
authz_bypass_raw_uri_check.risk: An access-control check compares the raw, un-normalized request URI (getRequestURI()) against a protected path prefix. Extra slashes, path segments like "..;", or percent-encoding can make the raw URI differ from the path actually dispatched to the handler, bypassing the check while still reaching the protected resource — CWE-863 (Advanced Path Normalization authorization bypass, as seen in several servlet-container and framework CVEs).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Normalize the path before comparing (StringUtils.cleanPath, or compare against the framework's resolved/dispatched path, not the raw URI), and reject requests containing suspicious sequences like ";" or "%2e%2e" before authorization checks run.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

authz_bypass_raw_uri_check.benefit: Closes a well-documented class of authorization-filter bypass caused by inconsistent path normalization between the security layer and the dispatcher.

cleartext_storage_class.title: Secret stored in a plain String field
cleartext_storage_class.risk: Storing a sensitive value (password, token, secret) as a plaintext String field in a class allows it to persist in JVM memory, heap dumps, thread dumps, and serialized objects — once stored in a String, the value cannot be zeroed from memory and may linger in the JVM string pool (CWE-499, CWE-312).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use char[] instead of String for sensitive data — char arrays can be zeroed after use (Arrays.fill(password, '\\0')). Better yet, use a SecretKey object (javax.crypto.SecretKey) or avoid storing credentials in memory longer than necessary.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_storage_class.benefit: Prevents sensitive data exposure via heap dumps and JVM memory inspection.

cleartext_storage_cookie.title: Secret stored in a cookie
cleartext_storage_cookie.risk: Storing a sensitive value (password, token, secret) directly as a cookie value transmits it to the client in cleartext — cookies are visible in browser devtools, proxies, and server access logs. If the Secure flag is not set, they also travel over unencrypted HTTP (CWE-312, CWE-315).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never store raw sensitive values in cookies. Store only opaque session identifiers in cookies; retrieve actual sensitive data server-side from a session store.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_storage_cookie.benefit: Prevents sensitive data exposure via cookie content visible to clients and intermediaries.

cleartext_storage_properties.title: Secret hardcoded in a Properties object
cleartext_storage_properties.risk: Hardcoding sensitive values (passwords, API keys) directly into Java Properties objects creates a cleartext credential in the source code — committed to version control, visible in compiled .class files via decompilation, and cannot be rotated without a code change (CWE-312).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Load sensitive values from environment variables (System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD")) or a secrets manager. Use a configuration framework that supports encrypted properties (Jasypt, Spring Cloud Config).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_storage_properties.benefit: Prevents credential exposure via source code and compiled class file decompilation.

command_injection_java_broad.title: Command Injection (Java)
command_injection_java_broad.risk: System command executed in a file containing HTTP request parameters — potential command injection (CWE-78).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Avoid passing user input to system commands. Use parameterized APIs instead of shell execution.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

command_injection_java_broad.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

comparison_wider_type.title: Loop comparison with a wider type
comparison_wider_type.risk: Comparing an int loop variable against a long or wider value (e.g., array.length cast to long) in a loop condition loses precision — if the long value exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE, the int variable never reaches it, creating an infinite loop or off-by-one error exploitable for denial of service (CWE-190, CWE-197).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Ensure both sides of the loop comparison have compatible types. Cast the wider type to int after validating it fits, or use a long loop variable if the range may exceed int bounds.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

comparison_wider_type.benefit: Prevents infinite loops and off-by-one errors caused by type width mismatch in loop conditions.

conditional_bypass_java.title: Security decision based on user input (Java)
conditional_bypass_java.risk: A security-sensitive conditional that directly tests user-supplied input to decide whether to authenticate or authorize access can be bypassed — an attacker crafts the request parameter to satisfy the condition, gaining access without legitimate credentials (CWE-807, CWE-290).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never base authentication or authorization decisions on raw user-supplied values. Verify credentials against a trusted data store (database, LDAP) and use server-side session state to track authentication status.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

conditional_bypass_java.benefit: Prevents authentication bypass via user-controlled security conditions.

dangerous_function_java.title: Runtime.exec() with user input
dangerous_function_java.risk: Calling Runtime.exec() with arguments derived from user input allows OS command injection — an attacker can inject shell metacharacters or additional commands to execute arbitrary OS commands with the JVM's process privileges (CWE-676, CWE-078).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use ProcessBuilder with an explicit argument array: new ProcessBuilder("cmd", arg1, arg2). Each argument is passed to the OS without shell interpretation. Validate all arguments against an allowlist.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

dangerous_function_java.benefit: Prevents OS command injection by using ProcessBuilder with explicit argument arrays.

db_error_exposed_java.title: DB error exposed in response (Java)
db_error_exposed_java.risk: A database or application exception message is returned directly in the HTTP response. Error output can reveal table names, column names, SQL query structure, library versions, or internal class paths — information that helps attackers craft targeted exploits (CWE-209).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Return a generic error message and HTTP 500 status to the client. Log the full exception server-side with a logging framework (SLF4J, Logback). Use a @ControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler to centralize error handling and prevent accidental detail leakage.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_error_exposed_java.benefit: Prevents database reconnaissance that enables targeted SQL injection and data extraction attacks.

db_superuser_connection_java.title: DB connection as superuser (Java)
db_superuser_connection_java.risk: A JDBC connection uses a privileged account (root, sa, admin, postgres). Connecting with a superuser grants all database privileges — a compromised application can read, modify, or delete any data and database objects (CWE-250).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Create a dedicated database user with only the minimum permissions required by the application (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on specific tables). Store credentials in environment variables or a secrets manager, never in source code.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_superuser_connection_java.benefit: Limits blast radius of a compromised application to only the tables and operations the service needs.

db_tls_disabled_java.title: DB connection without TLS (Java)
db_tls_disabled_java.risk: The JDBC connection has SSL/TLS disabled or certificate verification turned off. All database traffic (queries, results, credentials) is transmitted in cleartext and can be intercepted on the network (CWE-327).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Enable SSL/TLS and certificate verification. For MySQL JDBC: append ?useSSL=true&verifyServerCertificate=true&requireSSL=true to the URL. For PostgreSQL JDBC: add ?ssl=true&sslmode=verify-full. Configure the server certificate in a Java truststore.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_tls_disabled_java.benefit: Encrypts all data in transit between the Java application and the database, preventing credential theft and data interception.

exec_relative_path.title: Command run through a relative path
exec_relative_path.risk: Executing a command with a relative path (no leading slash) relies on the PATH environment variable to locate the executable — an attacker who can modify PATH can substitute a malicious binary, redirecting execution to arbitrary code (CWE-078, CWE-088).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always use absolute paths for executables: Runtime.getRuntime().exec("/usr/bin/convert"). Alternatively, use ProcessBuilder with an absolute path and an explicit argument array.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

exec_relative_path.benefit: Prevents PATH manipulation attacks substituting trusted executables with malicious ones.

exec_tainted_environment.title: Command built from environment values
exec_tainted_environment.risk: Building a shell command from environment variables or system properties that can be influenced by external input allows command injection — in containerized or cloud environments, environment variables may be injected via CI/CD pipelines, configuration management, or compromised dependency injection (CWE-078, CWE-088, CWE-454).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate environment variable values against a strict allowlist before using them in commands. Pass values as explicit arguments to ProcessBuilder rather than embedding in command strings.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

exec_tainted_environment.benefit: Prevents command injection via externally controlled environment variables.

exec_unescaped.title: Command built by string concatenation
exec_unescaped.risk: Building a command string with concatenation before passing to Runtime.exec() allows shell metacharacter injection — any user-controlled segment can inject semicolons, pipes, or backticks to execute additional commands (CWE-078, CWE-088).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use ProcessBuilder with a separate argument array — each element is passed to the OS without shell interpretation: new ProcessBuilder("cmd", arg1, arg2).start().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

exec_unescaped.benefit: Prevents shell command injection via metacharacter injection in concatenated command strings.

groovy_injection.title: Groovy script injection
groovy_injection.risk: Evaluating a user-controlled Groovy script with GroovyShell.evaluate() or GroovyClassLoader executes arbitrary code with the JVM's full permissions — an attacker can read files, execute OS commands, open network connections, or load arbitrary classes (CWE-094).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never evaluate user-supplied Groovy scripts. If dynamic calculation is required, use a restricted expression language (JEXL with SecurityManager, Expression4J) or a validated formula engine. Apply a SecurityManager to restrict filesystem and network access if dynamic scripting is unavoidable.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

groovy_injection.benefit: Prevents arbitrary code execution via Groovy script injection.

hardcoded_connection_string_java.title: Hardcoded DB credentials (Java)
hardcoded_connection_string_java.risk: A JDBC connection uses a hardcoded password literal or a URL with embedded credentials. Credentials hardcoded in source code appear in version control history and can be extracted by anyone with repository access (CWE-798).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Read database credentials from environment variables or a secrets manager: String url = System.getenv("DB_URL"); String pass = System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD"); In Spring Boot, use application.properties with ${DB_PASSWORD} placeholder backed by environment variables or Vault.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

hardcoded_connection_string_java.benefit: Prevents database credential exposure via source code and version control history.

http_response_splitting.title: HTTP response splitting
http_response_splitting.risk: Setting HTTP response headers directly from user input allows HTTP Response Splitting — an attacker who injects CR+LF characters (\\r\\n) into the header value can inject arbitrary additional headers, split the response into two, enabling XSS, cache poisoning, or cross-user data leakage (CWE-113).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Strip or reject CR (\\r) and LF (\\n) characters from all values placed in HTTP headers. Use response.sendRedirect() only with validated URLs from an allowlist.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

http_response_splitting.benefit: Prevents HTTP Response Splitting attacks via CRLF injection in header values.

http_smuggling_trailer_trust.title: Chunked trailers trusted as headers
http_smuggling_trailer_trust.risk: Chunked-transfer trailer fields are copied into the main request/response header map without re-validation. A front-end proxy that sanitizes headers before forwarding the request won't see values injected via trailers, letting an attacker smuggle headers past security controls (front-end/back-end interpretation mismatch — CWE-444, HTTP Request/Response Smuggling).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never merge trailer fields into the primary header map used for security decisions. If trailers must be exposed, keep them in a clearly separate namespace, validate them against the same allowlist as regular headers, and never let them override an already-processed header.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

http_smuggling_trailer_trust.benefit: Prevents request/response smuggling attacks that rely on front-end and back-end components disagreeing about which headers are present.

infinite_loop_user_input.title: Loop exit controlled by user input
infinite_loop_user_input.risk: A loop whose exit condition depends on user-controlled input can be made to never terminate — an attacker crafts input that keeps the condition satisfied indefinitely, consuming 100% CPU and causing denial of service (CWE-835).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never use raw user input as a loop termination condition. Validate and bound loop iterations: apply a maximum iteration count, use server-side computed exit conditions, and add a circuit breaker.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

infinite_loop_user_input.benefit: Prevents denial-of-service via user-controlled loop termination conditions.

insecure_basic_auth.title: Basic authentication over HTTP
insecure_basic_auth.risk: Sending HTTP Basic Authentication credentials over plain HTTP (not HTTPS) transmits the Base64-encoded username and password in cleartext — any network observer can trivially decode the Base64 and extract the credentials (CWE-522, CWE-319).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always use HTTPS (TLS) when transmitting Basic Authentication credentials. Replace http:// URLs with https:// for all authenticated endpoints.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_basic_auth.benefit: Prevents credential interception by ensuring authentication credentials are transmitted only over encrypted HTTPS.

insecure_bean_validation.title: User input in Bean Validation messages
insecure_bean_validation.risk: Bean Validation constraint messages that include user-controlled values via EL expressions (${userInput}) in the message attribute are vulnerable to server-side template injection — the EL evaluator processes the expression and can execute arbitrary code (CWE-094).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use static, hardcoded validation messages. Never include user input in constraint message expressions. Use message bundles (properties files) for internationalization.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_bean_validation.benefit: Prevents EL injection via Bean Validation constraint message expressions.

insecure_cookie_flag.title: Insecure Cookie Flag
insecure_cookie_flag.risk: Cookie with Secure flag set to false is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections (CWE-614).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Set cookie.setSecure(true) to ensure cookies are only sent over HTTPS.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_cookie_flag.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

insecure_javamail.title: JavaMail without TLS
insecure_javamail.risk: Configuring JavaMail (javax.mail / jakarta.mail) with SMTP authentication enabled but without STARTTLS or SSL/TLS transmits the username and password in cleartext — any network observer can intercept the credentials (CWE-297, CWE-522).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Enable STARTTLS (props.put("mail.smtp.starttls.enable", "true")) or use SSL (props.put("mail.smtp.ssl.enable", "true")) when using SMTP authentication.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_javamail.benefit: Ensures SMTP credentials are transmitted only over encrypted connections.

insecure_ldap_auth.title: LDAP simple authentication without encryption
insecure_ldap_auth.risk: LDAP authentication with SECURITY_AUTHENTICATION set to "simple" over an unencrypted ldap:// connection transmits credentials in cleartext — any network observer can capture and replay the credentials. Simple bind over LDAP is equivalent to sending a password in plaintext (CWE-522, CWE-319).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use ldaps:// (LDAP over TLS) or STARTTLS. Set SECURITY_AUTHENTICATION to "simple" only over encrypted connections. Consider using SASL/GSSAPI for stronger authentication.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_ldap_auth.benefit: Prevents LDAP credential interception over unencrypted network connections.

insecure_maven_dependency.title: Maven repository over HTTP
insecure_maven_dependency.risk: A Maven repository declared with an HTTP (non-TLS) URL downloads artifacts over an unencrypted connection — a man-in-the-middle attacker can replace any downloaded .jar with a malicious version that runs with the application's full JVM privileges during build or at runtime (CWE-829, CWE-494).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Replace all repository URLs with HTTPS equivalents. Maven Central and most public repositories support HTTPS. Remove any HTTP repository declarations and configure Maven to block insecure HTTP repositories (maven.wagon.rto).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_maven_dependency.benefit: Prevents man-in-the-middle attacks replacing Maven artifacts with malicious code.

insufficient_key_size_java.title: RSA or DSA key too short (Java)
insufficient_key_size_java.risk: An RSA or DSA key with fewer than 2048 bits provides insufficient cryptographic strength — 512-bit RSA has been publicly broken, and 1024-bit RSA is approaching practical feasibility with current hardware. Keys below 2048 bits do not meet NIST minimum requirements (CWE-326).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use at least 2048-bit RSA keys (keyPairGenerator.initialize(2048)); prefer 4096-bit for long-lived keys. Consider using EC keys (P-256, P-384) for equivalent security with shorter key length.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insufficient_key_size_java.benefit: Ensures asymmetric keys meet minimum cryptographic strength requirements.

jexl_injection.title: JEXL expression injection
jexl_injection.risk: Evaluating a user-controlled JEXL (Java Expression Language) expression can execute arbitrary code — JEXL supports method calls, property access, and class loading, enabling attackers to call Runtime.exec() or load arbitrary classes (CWE-094).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never evaluate user-supplied JEXL expressions. If dynamic expressions are needed, use a sandbox configuration that restricts accessible classes and methods. Apply JexlSandbox to whitelist only the minimum required operations.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

jexl_injection.benefit: Prevents arbitrary code execution via JEXL expression injection.

ldap_injection_java_broad.title: LDAP Injection (Java)
ldap_injection_java_broad.risk: LDAP query executed in a file containing HTTP request parameters — potential LDAP injection (CWE-90).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use parameterized LDAP queries or escape special characters.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ldap_injection_java_broad.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

lock_order_inconsistency.title: Inconsistent lock order
lock_order_inconsistency.risk: Acquiring multiple locks in inconsistent order across different code paths can cause a deadlock — if thread A holds lock1 and waits for lock2 while thread B holds lock2 and waits for lock1, both threads block forever, creating a denial-of-service condition (CWE-833).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Always acquire locks in the same consistent order throughout the application. Document the lock ordering and enforce it by convention. Consider using java.util.concurrent utilities (ReentrantLock with tryLock timeout) to avoid deadlocks.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

lock_order_inconsistency.benefit: Prevents deadlock-based denial-of-service conditions in multithreaded applications.

log4shell_jndi.title: Log4Shell (JNDI)
log4shell_jndi.risk: JNDI lookups in log messages enable remote code execution via Log4j (CVE-2021-44228). Even in test/config files this is a red flag.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Update Log4j to 2.17+. Set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true. Remove all JNDI lookup patterns.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

log4shell_jndi.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

mass_assignment_java.title: Mass assignment (Java)
mass_assignment_java.risk: BeanUtils.copyProperties() or populate() with an HTTP request copies all request parameters onto the model object, including sensitive fields like role, isAdmin, or balance. An attacker can modify any property that maps to a request parameter (CWE-915).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use a DTO (Data Transfer Object) with only the fields the user should be able to set. Validate with @Valid and @ModelAttribute on explicitly declared DTOs. Use Spring Data's @JsonIgnore or Jackson's @JsonIgnoreProperties to exclude sensitive fields.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

mass_assignment_java.benefit: Prevents privilege escalation by ensuring only explicitly declared fields can be bound from HTTP requests.

missing_jwt_signature_check.title: JWT parsed without signature check
missing_jwt_signature_check.risk: Using Jwts.parser().parseClaimsJwt() instead of parseClaimsJws() skips signature verification — the JWT payload is accepted without verifying the cryptographic signature, allowing an attacker to forge any claims and bypass authentication or authorization (CWE-347).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always use parseClaimsJws() with a signing key: Jwts.parserBuilder().setSigningKey(signingKey).build().parseClaimsJws(token). This validates the signature before returning the claims.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_jwt_signature_check.benefit: Ensures JWT signature is cryptographically verified before trusting the claims.

missing_permission_check_java.title: Web action without permission check
missing_permission_check_java.risk: A web-exposed action method (a Jenkins-style "doXxx" endpoint or equivalent controller action) has no permission check at its start. Without an explicit checkPermission()/hasPermission() call, the action relies entirely on whatever coarse-grained access control is applied upstream — any user who can reach the URL can invoke it, regardless of the fine-grained permission the action actually requires (CWE-862, Missing Authorization).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Call the appropriate permission check (e.g. getTarget().checkPermission(MyPermission.CONFIGURE)) as the first statement of the action, before any side-effecting logic runs.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_permission_check_java.benefit: Ensures every web-exposed action enforces the specific permission it needs, instead of relying only on coarse-grained upstream access control.

mvel_injection.title: MVEL expression injection
mvel_injection.risk: Evaluating a user-controlled MVEL (MVFLEX Expression Language) expression enables arbitrary code execution — MVEL supports Java reflection and class instantiation, allowing attackers to execute OS commands via Runtime.exec() or load malicious classes (CWE-094).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never pass user input directly to MVEL.eval(). Use predefined, hardcoded expressions or a sandboxed evaluation context that restricts accessible classes.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

mvel_injection.benefit: Prevents arbitrary code execution via MVEL expression injection.

netty_bytebuf_leak_on_error.title: Netty ByteBuf not released on error
netty_bytebuf_leak_on_error.risk: A Netty ByteBuf (or similar reference-counted buffer) is retained with .retain() but no matching .release() is visible nearby, and there is no try/finally guarding it. If decoding fails partway (a malformed record, an unbalanced nested structure), the retained buffer is never released — an attacker who can trigger repeated decode failures exhausts pooled memory (CWE-401 / CWE-772, Missing Release of Resource).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Wrap the retain/use/release sequence in try/finally (or use ReferenceCountUtil.release() in a finally block) so the buffer is always released, including on the exception path triggered by malformed input.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

netty_bytebuf_leak_on_error.benefit: Prevents pooled-buffer memory exhaustion driven by repeated malformed input designed to hit the decode-failure path.

netty_response_splitting.title: HTTP response splitting (Netty)
netty_response_splitting.risk: Setting Netty HTTP response headers with user-controlled values allows HTTP Response Splitting — an attacker who injects CR+LF characters (\\r\\n) can inject additional headers, split the HTTP response, and manipulate subsequent responses in caches or proxies (CWE-113).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Strip or reject CR (\\r) and LF (\\n) characters from all values placed in HTTP headers. Netty has built-in header validation in newer versions; upgrade to a version with HttpHeaderValidationUtil enabled by default.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

netty_response_splitting.benefit: Prevents HTTP Response Splitting via CRLF injection in Netty HTTP headers.

nosql_document_parse_java.title: MongoDB Document.parse injection (Java)
nosql_document_parse_java.risk: Document.parse() or BasicDBObject.parse() called with a variable (not a string literal) can execute arbitrary MongoDB query operators if the variable contains user-controlled JSON. An attacker can inject $where, $regex, or $gt operators to bypass filters and extract unauthorized data (CWE-943).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never pass user input directly to Document.parse(). Build MongoDB filters using the Filters builder API with explicit field names and validated scalar values: Filters.eq("username", username). Use a schema validation library to whitelist allowed filter fields before parsing.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

nosql_document_parse_java.benefit: Prevents NoSQL injection that bypasses authentication and authorization filters via injected query operators.

numeric_cast_tainted.title: Narrowing cast of user input
numeric_cast_tainted.risk: Casting a user-supplied long or double to a narrower type (int, short, byte) silently truncates or wraps the value — if the result is used as an array index or financial amount, an attacker can provide a value like 2147483648 which wraps to -2147483648, causing negative index access or incorrect financial computations (CWE-681, CWE-190).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate the value is within the target type's range before casting. Use Math.toIntExact(longValue) which throws ArithmeticException on overflow.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

numeric_cast_tainted.benefit: Prevents numeric truncation attacks causing negative array indices or incorrect calculations.

ognl_injection.title: OGNL expression injection
ognl_injection.risk: Evaluating a user-controlled OGNL (Object-Graph Navigation Language) expression can execute arbitrary Java code — OGNL's @class@method() syntax allows calling static methods on any accessible class, enabling attackers to execute OS commands or load malicious classes. This is the attack vector behind the Struts2 critical RCE vulnerabilities (CWE-917).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never evaluate user-controlled OGNL expressions. Update Struts2 to the latest version which includes OGNL expression protection. Disable OGNL expression evaluation for user-provided values.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ognl_injection.benefit: Prevents remote code execution via OGNL expression injection (Struts2-style attacks).

partial_path_traversal.title: Partial path traversal
partial_path_traversal.risk: A path traversal guard using startsWith() without a trailing separator is bypassable — if the trusted directory is /safe/dir, then /safe/dir.evil/../secret passes the check because /safe/dir.evil starts with /safe/dir (CWE-023).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always append the file separator when comparing canonical paths: destFile.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(baseDir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

partial_path_traversal.benefit: Prevents path traversal bypass via directory name prefix matching without separator.

password_reversible_storage_java.title: Reversible password storage (Java)
password_reversible_storage_java.risk: A symmetric cipher (AES, DES, Blowfish) is used to store a password. Reversible encryption can be undone if the key is compromised — use a one-way hash instead (CWE-257).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use BCrypt, PBKDF2, or Argon2 for password storage. In Java, use Spring Security's BCryptPasswordEncoder or the jBCrypt library. Never use Cipher for password storage.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

password_reversible_storage_java.benefit: One-way hashing with a strong KDF makes stored passwords practically irrecoverable even after a database breach.

path_traversal_fis.title: Path Traversal (FileInputStream)
path_traversal_fis.risk: FileInputStream with user-controlled path allows directory traversal to read arbitrary files (CWE-22).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate and canonicalize file paths. Use Path.normalize().startsWith(basePath) to restrict access.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

path_traversal_fis.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

polynomial_redos_java.title: Regular expression open to ReDoS (Java)
polynomial_redos_java.risk: A regular expression with exponential backtracking complexity (nested quantifiers, e.g., (a+)+ or (.*){n,}) can be exploited to cause catastrophic backtracking — a carefully crafted input string causes the Java regex engine to retry exponentially many paths, pinning the CPU and creating a denial-of-service condition (CWE-730).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Rewrite the regex to avoid nested quantifiers. Use possessive quantifiers (a++) or atomic groups ((?>...)) to prevent backtracking. Test regexes with known ReDoS payloads before deployment.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

polynomial_redos_java.benefit: Prevents denial-of-service via catastrophically backtracking regular expressions.

predictable_seed.title: Predictable SecureRandom seed
predictable_seed.risk: Seeding a SecureRandom with a predictable or fixed value (timestamp, hardcoded bytes, constant) makes the generated numbers predictable — an attacker who knows or can guess the seed can reproduce all generated values, breaking session tokens, CSRF tokens, or cryptographic keys (CWE-335, CWE-337).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use the no-argument constructor: new SecureRandom() — the JVM seeds it from OS entropy sources (/dev/urandom or equivalent), which are cryptographically unpredictable.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

predictable_seed.benefit: Ensures SecureRandom is seeded with true entropy, making generated values cryptographically unpredictable.

regex_injection_java.title: Regex injection (Java)
regex_injection_java.risk: Compiling a user-controlled string as a regular expression allows an attacker to inject a catastrophically backtracking pattern, causing server CPU exhaustion (ReDoS) and denial of service (CWE-730, CWE-400).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never use raw user input as a regex pattern. Use Pattern.quote(userInput) to treat the user input as a literal string, or validate the input against an allowlist of known-safe patterns.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

regex_injection_java.benefit: Prevents ReDoS attacks via user-controlled regular expression patterns.

rsa_without_oaep.title: RSA without OAEP padding
rsa_without_oaep.risk: RSA encryption without OAEP padding (using plain "RSA" or "RSA/ECB/PKCS1Padding") is vulnerable to padding oracle attacks (PKCS#1 v1.5 Bleichenbacher attack) — an attacker who can query the decryption oracle can recover the plaintext in polynomial time (CWE-780).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use RSA with OAEP padding: Cipher.getInstance("RSA/ECB/OAEPWithSHA-256AndMGF1Padding"). OAEP is not vulnerable to the Bleichenbacher attack.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

rsa_without_oaep.benefit: Prevents padding oracle attacks against RSA-encrypted data.

session_fixation_java.title: Session fixation (Java)
session_fixation_java.risk: Code that establishes authentication (login/authenticate) does not renew the session identifier afterwards. If the session ID was known to an attacker before login (fixed via a link, a shared device, or a pre-authentication cookie), it remains valid after login — the attacker inherits the now-authenticated session (CWE-384, Session Fixation).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Regenerate the session identifier immediately after successful authentication (request.changeSessionId() in Servlet, or the framework's equivalent session-renewal call) so any pre-login session ID is invalidated.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

session_fixation_java.benefit: Prevents session fixation attacks where an attacker pre-sets a victim's session ID and hijacks it once the victim authenticates.

socket_auth_race.title: Race between socket accept and authentication
socket_auth_race.risk: Accepting a socket connection and performing authentication as separate non-atomic operations creates a race condition — if the implementation reads data from the socket before completing authentication, a second request can slip in between the accept() and the auth check, allowing unauthenticated data access (CWE-421).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Complete the full authentication handshake before reading any application data from the socket. Use SSL/TLS mutual authentication to delegate the auth to the protocol layer.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

socket_auth_race.benefit: Prevents unauthenticated data access via race condition between socket accept and authentication.

spring_actuator_exposed.title: Spring Actuator Exposed
spring_actuator_exposed.risk: /actuator/env exposes all configuration including secrets. /actuator/heapdump can leak credentials from memory (CWE-215).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Restrict to health and info only. Require authentication for all actuator endpoints.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

spring_actuator_exposed.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

sql_injection_java_broad.title: SQL Injection (Java)
sql_injection_java_broad.risk: SQL query executed in a file containing HTTP request parameters — potential SQL injection (CWE-89).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use parameterized queries with PreparedStatement and bound parameters.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sql_injection_java_broad.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

static_initialization_vector.title: Static initialization vector
static_initialization_vector.risk: Using a static, hardcoded initialization vector (IV) for AES-CBC or AES-GCM encryption defeats the purpose of the IV — the same plaintext will always produce the same ciphertext, enabling pattern analysis attacks. For GCM mode, IV reuse with the same key also breaks authentication, exposing the authentication key (CWE-329, CWE-1204).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Generate a fresh random IV for each encryption operation: byte[] iv = new byte[12]; new SecureRandom().nextBytes(iv); Prepend the IV to the ciphertext so it can be retrieved for decryption.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

static_initialization_vector.benefit: Ensures each encryption operation uses a unique IV, preventing pattern analysis and GCM authentication key exposure.

stored_procedure_dynamic_java.title: Dynamic stored procedure (Java)
stored_procedure_dynamic_java.risk: A stored procedure call is built by concatenating user-supplied values into an EXEC or CALL statement. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL or modify the procedure name and arguments to access unauthorized data (CWE-89).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use CallableStatement with parameterized placeholders: CallableStatement cs = conn.prepareCall("{call GetUser(?)}"); cs.setString(1, userName). Never build stored procedure calls by string concatenation with user input.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

stored_procedure_dynamic_java.benefit: Eliminates stored procedure injection by enforcing parameterized procedure calls.

taint_sensitive_attr_write.title: Sensitive attribute set from user input
taint_sensitive_attr_write.risk: An attacker can manipulate role or permission attributes by injecting crafted values, leading to privilege escalation and unauthorized access to restricted functionality.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never use user-supplied input to set security-sensitive attributes. Use server-side authorization checks and role assignments from a trusted data source (database, identity provider).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_sensitive_attr_write.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_trust_boundary.title: Trust boundary violation
taint_trust_boundary.risk: Unvalidated user input stored in the session can be trusted by later session-based checks, leading to privilege escalation, session fixation, or data tampering.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate and sanitize all user input before storing it in the HTTP session. Use typed values (int, enum) or allowlist checks rather than storing raw strings.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_trust_boundary.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

tainted_permissions_check.title: Permission check built from user input
tainted_permissions_check.risk: Using user-controlled input to construct a permission check argument allows privilege escalation — an attacker can craft a permission string that grants access to resources they should not be able to reach, bypassing the intended access control policy (CWE-807, CWE-290).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never pass user-controlled strings directly to permission checks. Use hardcoded, server-defined permission constants. Derive the permission to check from the action being performed, not from user input.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

tainted_permissions_check.benefit: Prevents privilege escalation via user-controlled permission check arguments.

temp_dir_info_disclosure.title: Predictable file in the temp directory
temp_dir_info_disclosure.risk: Creating files in java.io.tmpdir with predictable names can disclose application information — on shared systems, other users can read temp files created in the world-writable /tmp directory. On some JVM versions, the temp directory may also be world-readable (CWE-200).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use Files.createTempFile() which generates a unique name. Set restrictive permissions (PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rw-------")). Delete temp files explicitly after use.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

temp_dir_info_disclosure.benefit: Prevents information disclosure via world-readable temporary files in shared directories.

template_injection_java.title: Template injection (Java)
template_injection_java.risk: Passing user-controlled input to a Freemarker, Velocity, or Thymeleaf template engine for execution allows server-side template injection — attackers can use template directives to call Java reflection APIs, read environment variables, or execute OS commands (CWE-094, CWE-1336).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never use user input as a template string. Pass user data as template context variables, not as the template source. Pre-compile all templates at application startup from trusted files.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

template_injection_java.benefit: Prevents server-side template injection leading to arbitrary code execution.

toctou_race_condition.title: File check-then-use race (TOCTOU)
toctou_race_condition.risk: Checking file existence or permissions before operating on the file introduces a TOCTOU (time-of-check time-of-use) race condition — an attacker with write access to the directory can replace the file with a symlink between the check and the operation, causing the application to operate on an unintended file (CWE-367).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use atomic file operations. Open the file directly and handle the FileNotFoundException/NoSuchFileException rather than pre-checking existence. Use Files.createFile() with StandardOpenOption.CREATE_NEW for atomic creation.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

toctou_race_condition.benefit: Eliminates TOCTOU race condition between file existence check and file operation.

trust_boundary_java.title: Trust Boundary Violation
trust_boundary_java.risk: User input stored in HTTP session without validation crosses trust boundary (CWE-501).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate and sanitize all user input before storing in session.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

trust_boundary_java.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

unrestricted_file_upload_java.title: Unrestricted file upload (Java/Spring)
unrestricted_file_upload_java.risk: Spring MultipartFile.transferTo() or getOriginalFilename() without file type validation allows uploading of web shells, malware, and executable files (CWE-434, OWASP A04).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate file type via magic bytes (Apache Tika or Files.probeContentType), enforce a strict allowlist of extensions, and store files outside the web root with randomized names.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unrestricted_file_upload_java.benefit: Prevents web shell uploads and arbitrary code execution via unrestricted file upload (CWE-434).

url_forward_injection.title: Request forwarded to a user-controlled path
url_forward_injection.risk: Forwarding a request to an internal path derived from user input allows access to internal application resources that should not be exposed — an attacker can forward to /WEB-INF/web.xml, admin servlets, or internal API endpoints not meant for direct access (CWE-552).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use an allowlist of permitted forward destinations. Never derive internal forward paths from user input.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

url_forward_injection.benefit: Prevents unauthorized access to internal application resources via RequestDispatcher forwarding.

use_ssl_socket.title: Plain socket for sensitive data
use_ssl_socket.risk: Creating a plain java.net.Socket for connections that transmit sensitive data exposes the communication to network interception — all data including authentication credentials, session tokens, and business data is transmitted in cleartext (CWE-319).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use SSLSocket via SSLSocketFactory for client connections or SSLServerSocket for server sockets: SSLSocketFactory factory = (SSLSocketFactory) SSLSocketFactory.getDefault(); SSLSocket socket = (SSLSocket) factory.createSocket(host, port).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

use_ssl_socket.benefit: Ensures all socket communication is encrypted with TLS, preventing network eavesdropping.

weak_cipher_java.title: Weak Cipher (Java)
weak_cipher_java.risk: Weak cipher algorithm (DES, RC2, RC4) provides insufficient encryption strength (CWE-327).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for encryption.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

weak_cipher_java.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

weak_random_java_util.title: Weak Random (Java)
weak_random_java_util.risk: java.util.Random is not cryptographically secure. Predictable values enable session hijacking or token forgery (CWE-330).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use java.security.SecureRandom for security-sensitive operations.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

weak_random_java_util.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

world_writable_file_read.title: Read from a world-writable file
world_writable_file_read.risk: Reading from a file that has been made world-writable (setWritable(true, false)) is dangerous — any process on the system can modify or replace the file between the write permission being set and the read operation, allowing untrusted content injection (CWE-732).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Restrict file permissions to owner-only: file.setWritable(true, true) (owner-only writable). Never make security-sensitive files world-writable. Use Java NIO Files.setPosixFilePermissions() for fine-grained control.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

world_writable_file_read.benefit: Prevents content injection via world-writable files being modified between write permission grant and read operation.

xpath_injection_java_eval.title: XPath Injection (Java)
xpath_injection_java_eval.risk: XPath expression built with user input via string concatenation enables data extraction (CWE-643).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use parameterized XPath queries with XPathVariableResolver instead of string concatenation.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xpath_injection_java_eval.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

xslt_injection.title: XSLT injection
xslt_injection.risk: Performing an XSLT transformation with a user-controlled stylesheet can execute arbitrary Java code — XSLT processors support extension functions that call Java reflection APIs, enabling arbitrary method invocation and remote code execution (CWE-074).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Disable extension functions and external document access before transformation: factory.setFeature(XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, true). Never accept user-controlled XSLT stylesheets.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xslt_injection.benefit: Prevents remote code execution via malicious XSLT extension functions.

zip_slip.title: Zip Slip
zip_slip.risk: Using ZipEntry.getName() directly as a file path for extraction allows Zip Slip attacks — a malicious archive can contain entries with paths like "../../../etc/cron.d/backdoor" that extract files outside the target directory, potentially overwriting system files or configuration (CWE-022).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Canonicalize the resolved path and verify it starts with the destination directory path (followed by a separator): File destFile = new File(destDir, entry.getName()); if (!destFile.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(destDir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator)) throw new IOException("Zip Slip").
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

zip_slip.benefit: Prevents path traversal attacks via malicious archive entry names.

account_enumeration_response_differentia.title: Account enumeration through distinct responses
account_enumeration_response_differentia.risk: A login, password-reset, or magic-link endpoint returns a distinct response (a different status code or message) when the account does not exist, compared to when it does. This observable response discrepancy lets an attacker enumerate valid accounts by trying many identifiers and watching which ones get the "not found" response (CWE-204, Observable Response Discrepancy).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Return the same generic response ("If an account exists, an email has been sent") regardless of whether the account was found, and take a constant amount of time doing so.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

account_enumeration_response_differentia.benefit: Prevents attackers from building a list of valid accounts to target with credential-stuffing or phishing campaigns.

angularjs_insecure_url_whitelist.title: AngularJS URL whitelist too broad
angularjs_insecure_url_whitelist.risk: An AngularJS $sceDelegateProvider URL whitelist that includes broad wildcards (e.g., '**' or 'http://**.example.com/**') allows any URL matching the pattern — attackers can exploit this to load resources from attacker-controlled subdomains like http://attacker.example.com/malicious.js (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use specific, minimal URL patterns in the whitelist without leading wildcards. Prefer exact domain matches over wildcard subdomain patterns.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

angularjs_insecure_url_whitelist.benefit: Prevents resource loading from attacker-controlled domains via overly broad URL whitelists.

api_key_in_url.title: API Key in URL
api_key_in_url.risk: API keys in URLs are logged by web servers, proxies, and browsers (CWE-598).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Send API keys in the Authorization header, never in the URL.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

api_key_in_url.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

auth_truthy_check_ignores_error.title: Authentication check ignores the error
auth_truthy_check_ignores_error.risk: The code treats a truthy session/auth object as proof the user is authenticated, without checking for an error field. Some auth libraries populate the session object even on a configuration or verification failure and set an `error` property instead of returning null/undefined — code that only checks truthiness fails open and grants access despite the underlying check having failed (CWE-285, Improper Authorization).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Check both that the session object exists AND that it has no error field (e.g. if (session && !session.error)) before treating the user as authenticated.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

auth_truthy_check_ignores_error.benefit: Ensures authentication library errors result in access being denied, not silently accepted as a valid session.

bad_tag_filter.title: HTML tags filtered with a regex
bad_tag_filter.risk: Filtering HTML tags with regular expressions is an unreliable sanitization strategy — attackers bypass it with malformed tags (<scr<script>ipt>), nested tags, Unicode equivalents, or by breaking tags across multiple attributes. Regex-based HTML parsing is fundamentally broken (CWE-116, CWE-020, CWE-185).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use a dedicated HTML sanitization library (DOMPurify for client-side, sanitize-html or DOMPurify with jsdom for server-side) with an explicit allowlist of safe tags and attributes.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

bad_tag_filter.benefit: Ensures HTML sanitization is reliable and resistant to bypass via malformed or nested tags.

base64_eval.title: Base64 obfuscated code execution
base64_eval.risk: eval/exec on base64-decoded content hides malicious code to bypass security tools (CWE-506).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never execute base64-decoded code. Use JSON.parse for structured data.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

base64_eval.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

base64_obfuscation.title: Suspicious base64 string decoded
base64_obfuscation.risk: A long base64 string decoded by atob() may contain obfuscated malicious code (CWE-506).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Verify decoded content. Prefer readable formats (JSON, plain text).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

base64_obfuscation.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

broken_crypto_algorithm.title: Broken encryption algorithm
broken_crypto_algorithm.risk: DES, 3DES (Triple DES), RC2, RC4, and Blowfish are cryptographically broken or obsolete algorithms — DES has a 56-bit key trivially brute-forceable, RC4 has known statistical biases, and RC2 has known attacks. Using them provides no meaningful confidentiality protection (CWE-327).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use AES-256-GCM (crypto.createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", key, iv)) for symmetric encryption. AES-256-GCM provides authenticated encryption with a 256-bit key, currently unbroken.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

broken_crypto_algorithm.benefit: Replaces broken/obsolete ciphers with a modern, secure encryption algorithm.

buffer_index_without_bounds_check.title: Buffer read without bounds check
buffer_index_without_bounds_check.risk: A buffer is read at an offset derived from external/untrusted input (a request parameter, a computed index) with no visible bounds check against the buffer's actual length. An out-of-range offset causes an out-of-bounds read, potentially disclosing adjacent heap memory or crashing the process (CWE-125).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate the offset against the buffer's length before reading (offset >= 0 && offset + size <= buffer.length), and reject the request otherwise instead of letting the read proceed.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

buffer_index_without_bounds_check.benefit: Prevents out-of-bounds reads and the associated memory disclosure or crash when processing attacker-controlled offsets.

build_artifact_leak.title: Source maps published in production
build_artifact_leak.risk: Publishing source maps in a production build exposes the original application source code to anyone who downloads the map file — attackers can read business logic, API endpoints, secret hardcoded values, and internal architecture from the decompiled source (CWE-312, CWE-315, CWE-359).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Disable source maps in production builds. In webpack, set devtool: false for production. If source maps are needed for error tracking, upload them to your error tracking service (Sentry) and exclude them from the public bundle.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

build_artifact_leak.benefit: Prevents source code exposure via build artifact source maps in production deployments.

case_sensitive_middleware_path.title: Case-sensitive middleware path
case_sensitive_middleware_path.risk: Express middleware registered on a path like "/admin" uses case-sensitive matching by default, but the underlying route handler may use case-insensitive matching — a request to "/ADMIN" or "/Admin" bypasses the middleware security check (authentication, rate limiting) while still reaching the route (CWE-178).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Apply security middleware broadly (before route registration) rather than on specific paths, or normalize path casing in a preliminary middleware.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

case_sensitive_middleware_path.benefit: Prevents security middleware bypass via path case variation.

cleartext_cookie.title: Sensitive cookie without Secure flag
cleartext_cookie.risk: A cookie containing a sensitive value (token, password) set without the Secure flag transmits the value over unencrypted HTTP connections, where it can be intercepted by network observers (CWE-614, CWE-311, CWE-312).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always set sensitive cookies with Secure: true, HttpOnly: true, and SameSite: "Strict" or "Lax". The Secure flag prevents the cookie from being sent over HTTP.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_cookie.benefit: Prevents cookie interception over unencrypted HTTP connections.

cleartext_logging.title: Sensitive data logged in cleartext
cleartext_logging.risk: Logging sensitive values (passwords, tokens, secrets) writes them in cleartext to log files, log aggregation systems, and stdout — logs are often retained long-term, accessible to monitoring tools, and may be stored insecurely in cloud logging services (CWE-312, CWE-315, CWE-359).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never log raw sensitive values. Mask or redact sensitive fields before logging: log the presence ("token present: true"), not the value. Use structured logging with field-level redaction.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_logging.benefit: Prevents sensitive data exposure via application log files and log aggregation systems.

cleartext_storage_sensitive.title: Sensitive data in browser storage
cleartext_storage_sensitive.risk: Storing sensitive data (passwords, tokens, secrets) in localStorage or sessionStorage writes them in plaintext accessible to any JavaScript on the page — XSS can read all localStorage entries, and the data persists across browser restarts in localStorage (CWE-312, CWE-315, CWE-359).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never store passwords or raw tokens in localStorage. Use HTTP-only cookies for session tokens (inaccessible to JavaScript). For short-lived tokens, prefer in-memory storage (JavaScript variable in a closure) or sessionStorage with awareness of its limitations.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cleartext_storage_sensitive.benefit: Prevents XSS-based credential theft from client-side storage.

client_side_ssrf.title: Client-side request forgery
client_side_ssrf.risk: Making an HTTP request to a URL derived from DOM properties (window.location, document.URL) can be exploited for client-side request forgery — an attacker can craft a URL that causes the browser to make requests to unintended destinations, leaking credentials or CSRF tokens to third-party servers (CWE-918).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate the URL before making the request. Ensure the hostname matches an allowlist of expected API endpoints. Never construct request URLs from untrusted DOM properties without validation.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

client_side_ssrf.benefit: Prevents client-side request forgery via DOM-derived request URLs.

conditional_bypass.title: Security decision based on user input
conditional_bypass.risk: A security-sensitive conditional that directly compares user-controlled data (from request body, params, or query) against a privileged value can be bypassed by an attacker who crafts the request to satisfy the condition (CWE-807, CWE-290).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never base authorization decisions on user-supplied values. Use a server-side session or JWT claims to determine privileges. Validate roles from a trusted data source (database, identity provider), not from the request itself.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

conditional_bypass.benefit: Prevents authorization bypass via user-controlled security conditions.

cors_credentials_wildcard.title: CORS wildcard with credentials
cors_credentials_wildcard.risk: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * combined with credentials: true is rejected by browsers but indicates misconfiguration (CWE-942).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Explicitly specify allowed origins instead of wildcard.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cors_credentials_wildcard.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

cross_tenant_resource_access.title: Resource accessed across tenants
cross_tenant_resource_access.risk: A resource is looked up by its own ID without also scoping the query to the caller's workspace/organization/tenant. In a multi-tenant app this lets any authenticated user read or modify another tenant's data (cross-workspace IDOR) — CWE-863.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Always include the caller's tenant/workspace ID in the lookup query, e.g. findOne({ _id: id, workspaceId: req.user.workspaceId }). Never trust an object ID alone to scope access in a multi-tenant system.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cross_tenant_resource_access.benefit: Prevents cross-tenant data leakage and modification in multi-tenant applications.

crud_without_ownership.title: CRUD without ownership check
crud_without_ownership.risk: Users can access or modify resources belonging to other users (IDOR).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Verify resource ownership before every CRUD operation.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

crud_without_ownership.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

data_uri_html.title: Data URI with HTML content
data_uri_html.risk: data:text/html allows injecting executable HTML/JS in an iframe or image (CWE-79).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Forbid data: URIs with text/html. Validate and sanitize sources.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

data_uri_html.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

db_connection_string_credentials_js.title: DB connection string with credentials (JavaScript)
