db_connection_string_credentials_js.risk: A database connection URL with embedded credentials (protocol://user:password@host/db) stores plaintext secrets in source code. These credentials appear in version control history and can be extracted by anyone with repository access (CWE-798).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Store the connection URL in an environment variable: const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL. Use a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault) in production. Add .env files to .gitignore and never commit them.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_connection_string_credentials_js.benefit: Prevents database credential exposure via source code and version control history.

db_tls_disabled_js.title: DB connection without TLS (JavaScript)
db_tls_disabled_js.risk: TLS is disabled or certificate validation is bypassed for a database connection. All traffic (queries, results, authentication tokens) is sent in cleartext, exposing it to network interception (CWE-327).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Set ssl: true and rejectUnauthorized: true (the default). Provide a valid CA certificate. For pg: { ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: fs.readFileSync('/etc/ssl/ca.crt').toString() } }. For mongoose: tls: true.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_tls_disabled_js.benefit: Ensures all database communications are encrypted and the server identity is verified, preventing man-in-the-middle attacks.

dependency_confusion.title: Dependency Confusion
dependency_confusion.risk: If an internal package name exists on public npm, an attacker can publish a malicious version (CWE-427).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use npm scoped packages (@company/pkg). Configure .npmrc with registry for your scope.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

dependency_confusion.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

different_kinds_comparison_bypass.title: Security check comparing different request fields
different_kinds_comparison_bypass.risk: Comparing two different kinds of HTTP request data (e.g., query parameter vs body field) as a security check can be bypassed — an attacker who controls both input channels can make them equal trivially, defeating the security intent (CWE-807, CWE-290).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use a server-side secret for security comparisons (e.g., CSRF tokens should be generated server-side and stored in the session, not compared between user-controlled inputs).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

different_kinds_comparison_bypass.benefit: Prevents security check bypass via attacker-controlled comparison of different request data kinds.

disable_certificate_validation.title: TLS certificate validation disabled
disable_certificate_validation.risk: Setting rejectUnauthorized: false or NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 disables TLS certificate validation entirely — HTTPS connections accept any certificate, including self-signed and expired ones, making the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks (CWE-295, CWE-297).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove rejectUnauthorized: false. If connecting to a server with a self-signed certificate, add the CA certificate to the ca option instead of disabling validation entirely.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

disable_certificate_validation.benefit: Ensures TLS certificate chain is validated, preventing man-in-the-middle attacks.

dom_pseudo_eval.title: String passed to setTimeout or setInterval
dom_pseudo_eval.risk: Passing a string (especially a dynamically constructed one) to setTimeout() or setInterval() causes the JavaScript engine to evaluate it as code — equivalent to eval(), allowing code injection if any user-controlled data is embedded in the string (CWE-094, CWE-079).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always pass a function reference to setTimeout/setInterval, never a string. Use an arrow function or named function if parameters are needed.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

dom_pseudo_eval.benefit: Prevents code injection via string-based setTimeout/setInterval usage.

double_escaping.title: Double escaping or unescaping
double_escaping.risk: Un-escaping HTML entities after previously escaping them (e.g., replacing & back to &) can lead to double-escaping or incomplete sanitization — if only some entities are un-escaped, the result is inconsistent and may allow crafted input to escape the sanitization (CWE-116, CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Avoid manual entity manipulation chains. Use a single, consistent escaping/unescaping library and apply it only once. Never un-escape HTML entities in a security-sensitive context.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

double_escaping.benefit: Prevents inconsistent sanitization caused by double-escaping or mismatched escape/unescape operations.

electron_insecure_content.title: Electron allows insecure content
electron_insecure_content.risk: Setting allowRunningInsecureContent: true in Electron allows HTTP-loaded active content (scripts, plugins) to run in an HTTPS context — a man-in-the-middle attacker can inject malicious scripts that execute with the privileges of the Electron renderer, potentially reaching Node.js APIs (CWE-494).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove allowRunningInsecureContent: true. Load all resources over HTTPS. Never mix HTTP and HTTPS content in Electron applications.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

electron_insecure_content.benefit: Prevents MITM injection of malicious scripts via mixed HTTP/HTTPS content in Electron.

electron_node_integration.title: Electron nodeIntegration enabled
electron_node_integration.risk: Enabling nodeIntegration: true in Electron exposes the full Node.js API to renderer processes — if any renderer loads untrusted web content (via XSS, navigation, or remote content), that content can execute arbitrary shell commands and access the filesystem with OS-level privileges (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Set nodeIntegration: false and contextIsolation: true. Use the contextBridge API to expose only specific safe IPC methods to the renderer instead of the full Node.js API.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

electron_node_integration.benefit: Prevents XSS in renderer from escalating to OS-level code execution via Node.js API access.

electron_web_security_disabled.title: Electron webSecurity disabled
electron_web_security_disabled.risk: Setting webSecurity: false in an Electron BrowserWindow disables the Same-Origin Policy, HTTPS certificate validation, and mixed content blocking — any web content loaded in the window can make arbitrary cross-origin requests, read local files, and execute arbitrary code with Node.js privileges (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove webSecurity: false. If cross-origin access is needed for development, use proper CORS headers or a proxy. In production, always keep webSecurity enabled.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

electron_web_security_disabled.benefit: Maintains browser security boundaries preventing arbitrary cross-origin requests in Electron apps.

empty_password_config.title: Empty password in configuration
empty_password_config.risk: An empty or null password in configuration means no authentication is required to access the resource (database, Redis, API) — any client can connect without credentials, enabling unauthorized data access (CWE-258, CWE-862).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Set a strong, non-empty password for all services. Load the password from an environment variable (process.env.DB_PASSWORD) and fail startup if it is not set.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

empty_password_config.benefit: Ensures all services require authentication, preventing unauthorized access.

eval_template_literal.title: eval() with template literal
eval_template_literal.risk: eval() with a template literal allows arbitrary code execution (CWE-94).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never use eval(). Use safe alternatives (JSON.parse, isolated Function constructor).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

eval_template_literal.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

express_no_csrf.title: Express without CSRF protection
express_no_csrf.risk: POST/PUT/DELETE routes without CSRF middleware are vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CWE-352).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add csurf or lusca as CSRF middleware.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

express_no_csrf.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

file_access_to_http.title: Local file sent in an HTTP request
file_access_to_http.risk: Directly reading a file from the filesystem and sending its contents in an outbound HTTP request may indicate information disclosure — if the file path is user-influenced, an attacker may be able to exfiltrate arbitrary local files to an external server (CWE-200).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
If file data must be sent to an external service, ensure the file path is fixed (not user-influenced), the external endpoint is explicitly trusted, and only the necessary data is transmitted.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

file_access_to_http.benefit: Prevents unauthorized exfiltration of local file contents to external servers.

filesystem_race_condition.title: File system race condition (TOCTOU)
filesystem_race_condition.risk: Checking a file's existence or permissions with fs.exists()/fs.access() before operating on it introduces a TOCTOU (time-of-check time-of-use) race condition — an attacker can replace the file with a symlink between the check and the operation, causing the application to operate on an unintended file (CWE-367).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use atomic operations: open the file directly with O_EXCL flag for creation, or handle the error from the operation itself rather than pre-checking existence. The error-first approach is atomic.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

filesystem_race_condition.benefit: Eliminates TOCTOU race condition on file system operations.

functionality_untrusted_domain.title: External script without Subresource Integrity
functionality_untrusted_domain.risk: Loading JavaScript or other active content from an external domain without Subresource Integrity (SRI) allows that domain to inject arbitrary code into your page — if the domain is compromised, misconfigured, or serves different content, your users run attacker-controlled code (CWE-830).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add integrity= and crossorigin= attributes (Subresource Integrity) to all external script and link tags. Generate the hash with: cat file.js | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

functionality_untrusted_domain.benefit: Prevents code injection via compromised or replaced external script sources.

functionality_untrusted_source.title: Script or stylesheet loaded over HTTP
functionality_untrusted_source.risk: Loading scripts or stylesheets from external sources over HTTP exposes the application to man-in-the-middle attacks — an attacker can intercept and replace the resource with malicious code that executes in the context of your page, leading to full XSS compromise (CWE-830).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Load external resources exclusively over HTTPS. Use Subresource Integrity (SRI) attributes (integrity= and crossorigin=) to cryptographically verify the content of external scripts and stylesheets.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

functionality_untrusted_source.benefit: Prevents man-in-the-middle injection of malicious scripts via external resource loading.

graphql_batching_attack.title: GraphQL Batching Attack
graphql_batching_attack.risk: An attacker can send thousands of operations in a single batched request, causing DoS or brute-forcing authentication (CWE-770).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Disable batching or limit batch size. Add query cost analysis and rate limiting.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

graphql_batching_attack.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

hardcoded_data_as_code.title: Encoded data executed as code
hardcoded_data_as_code.risk: Executing code that was encoded as hexadecimal, base64, or Unicode escape sequences is a technique strongly associated with backdoors and obfuscated malware — the encoding hides the true intent from static analysis and code review (CWE-506).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Avoid evaluating encoded data as code. If dynamic code execution is truly needed, use a sandboxed execution environment (vm2, isolated-vm) with strict resource limits. Prefer static code that can be reviewed directly.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

hardcoded_data_as_code.benefit: Prevents obfuscated backdoor code from hiding malicious intent via data encoding.

host_header_poisoning.title: Host header poisoning
host_header_poisoning.risk: Using the HTTP Host header to construct links in password reset or confirmation emails allows an attacker to poison the header value, making the link point to an attacker-controlled server — enabling credential theft and account takeover (CWE-640).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use a hardcoded base URL from application configuration (environment variable) for link generation, never derive it from the Host header.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

host_header_poisoning.benefit: Prevents account takeover via Host header poisoning in transactional emails.

http_to_file_access.title: HTTP data written to a file
http_to_file_access.risk: Writing HTTP response data directly to the file system without validation allows an attacker who controls the response (via MITM or a malicious server) to write arbitrary files — enabling backdoor installation, configuration overwrite, or arbitrary file upload (CWE-912, CWE-434).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate the content type and size of the HTTP response before writing. Use a fixed, allowlisted output path. Verify cryptographic checksums when downloading executable content.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

http_to_file_access.benefit: Prevents arbitrary file write via unvalidated HTTP response data.

ide_config_exfil.title: Write to IDE or AI assistant configuration
ide_config_exfil.risk: Code writes into an IDE/AI assistant configuration file under .claude/, .vscode/, .cursor/, .aider/ or .codeium/. The TanStack/Mistral npm supply-chain attack (May 2026) created .claude/settings.json and .vscode/tasks.json as persistence vectors that re-execute the malicious payload at every IDE startup. Legitimate code does not silently rewrite a user's editor configuration during install.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Audit the surrounding code: legitimate setup scripts ask explicit consent before modifying user IDE/AI tool settings. If unsure, isolate the package in a sandbox and inspect tarball contents before re-installing.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

ide_config_exfil.benefit: Detects a documented persistence vector used in npm supply-chain attacks and blocks silent IDE/AI tool reconfiguration.

improper_code_sanitization.title: Code sanitized by string replace before eval
improper_code_sanitization.risk: Sanitizing input with string replace before passing to eval() or new Function() is insufficient — attackers bypass simple sanitizers by exploiting encoding, nested quotes, or Unicode characters that the sanitizer misses while the JavaScript engine processes them (CWE-094).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never pass user input to eval() or new Function(), even after sanitization. Use a proper sandboxed evaluation environment (vm2, isolated-vm) if dynamic code execution is truly required.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

improper_code_sanitization.benefit: Prevents code injection bypass via insufficient sanitization before eval.

incomplete_hostname_regexp.title: Hostname regex with an unescaped dot
incomplete_hostname_regexp.risk: A hostname regular expression with an unescaped dot matches broader patterns than intended — e.g., the pattern /evil.com/ also matches "notevil.com" or "evil-com.attacker.com", enabling hostname validation bypass (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Escape dots in hostname patterns (\\.instead of .) and anchor with ^ and $ or use word boundaries. Prefer URL.hostname property over regex validation.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_hostname_regexp.benefit: Prevents hostname validation bypass via lookalike domain names.

incomplete_html_attribute_sanitization.title: Incomplete HTML attribute sanitization
incomplete_html_attribute_sanitization.risk: Embedding user input in HTML attribute values without proper sanitization allows attribute injection — in href/src attributes, javascript: URIs can execute scripts; in event attributes (onclick, onerror), any JavaScript executes when the event fires (CWE-079, CWE-116, CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Sanitize attribute values with DOMPurify.sanitize() or a context-aware escaper. For href/src, validate against an allowlist of safe schemes (https://, /) before insertion.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_html_attribute_sanitization.benefit: Prevents XSS via HTML attribute injection including javascript: URIs and event handler injection.

incomplete_multichar_sanitization.title: Incomplete multi-character sanitization
incomplete_multichar_sanitization.risk: Replacing multi-character dangerous sequences (like "<script>") as plain strings removes only exact-case matches — an attacker bypasses with "<Script>", "<SCRIPT>", "jAvAsCrIpT:", or by splitting the pattern across multiple replace calls (CWE-116, CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use case-insensitive global regex replacements (/pattern/gi) for dangerous patterns, or better yet, use a dedicated sanitization library (DOMPurify, sanitize-html) that handles all variants.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_multichar_sanitization.benefit: Prevents XSS bypass via case variations of dangerous HTML/JavaScript sequences.

incomplete_sanitization.title: replace() without the global flag
incomplete_sanitization.risk: String.replace() without the global flag /g replaces only the first occurrence of the metacharacter — an attacker using multiple occurrences (e.g., "<sc<script>ript>") bypasses the sanitization completely (CWE-116, CWE-020, CWE-080).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use replace() with a global regex (e.g., replace(/</, "")) or a dedicated sanitization library (DOMPurify, validator). Better yet, avoid sanitization by design — use textContent instead of innerHTML.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_sanitization.benefit: Ensures all occurrences of dangerous characters are replaced, not just the first.

incomplete_url_scheme_check.title: Incomplete URL scheme check
incomplete_url_scheme_check.risk: Checking only for the "javascript:" scheme without also blocking "vbscript:" and "data:" leaves executable URL schemes unblocked — an attacker can inject "vbscript:alert(1)" or "data:text/html,<script>" to achieve XSS (CWE-020, CWE-184).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Block all executable URL schemes: check for javascript:, vbscript:, and data: (case-insensitively). Better yet, use an allowlist — only permit http: and https: schemes.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_url_scheme_check.benefit: Prevents XSS via alternative executable URL schemes bypassing incomplete scheme checks.

incomplete_url_substring_sanitization.title: URL checked by substring
incomplete_url_substring_sanitization.risk: URL validation using startsWith/endsWith/includes on a domain string is bypassable — "https://safe.com.attacker.com" passes a startsWith check for "https://safe.com", enabling open redirect or SSRF (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Parse the URL with new URL(href) and validate the hostname property against an explicit allowlist. Never validate URLs by substring checks on the raw string.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incomplete_url_substring_sanitization.benefit: Prevents open redirect and SSRF via crafted URL substrings.

incorrect_suffix_check.title: Incorrect suffix check with indexOf
incorrect_suffix_check.risk: Using indexOf to simulate endsWith without handling the -1 case is incorrect — if the substring is not found, indexOf returns -1 and the comparison (str.indexOf(s) === str.length - s.length) is false, but when the string length equals the substring length minus one, the -1 maps to -1 === -1 and gives a false positive (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use the built-in String.prototype.endsWith() method or explicitly handle indexOf returning -1.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

incorrect_suffix_check.benefit: Prevents incorrect string validation logic that could allow filter bypass.

indirect_command_injection.title: Shell command built by concatenation
indirect_command_injection.risk: Building a shell command string via string concatenation or template literals creates a command injection vulnerability — an attacker who controls any segment can inject shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, $()) to execute arbitrary commands (CWE-078, CWE-088).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use spawn() with an argument array instead of exec() with a string: spawn("cmd", [arg1, arg2]) — each argument is passed directly without shell interpolation. If exec() is required, use execFile() with an array.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

indirect_command_injection.benefit: Prevents OS command injection via shell metacharacter injection in command strings.

inline_event_handler.title: Inline event handler
inline_event_handler.risk: on* attributes (onerror, onload, onclick) execute JavaScript without script tags, bypassing some CSP protections (CWE-79).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use addEventListener() instead of inline on* attributes.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

inline_event_handler.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

insecure_dependency_http.title: npm dependency over HTTP or FTP
insecure_dependency_http.risk: A dependency declared with an HTTP or FTP URL in package.json is fetched without TLS encryption, allowing a man-in-the-middle attacker to replace the package with malicious code that runs during npm install (CWE-300, CWE-319, CWE-494, CWE-829).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace HTTP/FTP dependency URLs with HTTPS equivalents, or better, publish the package to npm and reference it by name and version.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

insecure_dependency_http.benefit: Prevents man-in-the-middle attacks replacing npm dependencies with malicious code.

insecure_download.title: Executable downloaded over HTTP
insecure_download.risk: Downloading executable files or packages over HTTP (unencrypted) exposes the download to man-in-the-middle attacks — an attacker on the network path can replace the downloaded file with malicious code that executes with the application's privileges (CWE-829, CWE-300).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Use an explicit allowlist of permitted method names: const ALLOWED = ["read", "write"]; if (ALLOWED.includes(req.body.action)) obj[req.body.action](). Never directly index objects with user-supplied property names.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_dynamic_method_access.benefit: Prevents remote code execution via dynamic method invocation with user-controlled property names.

unsafe_reflection_from_deserialized_inpu.title: Class chosen from deserialized input
unsafe_reflection_from_deserialized_inpu.risk: A class/constructor is selected dynamically by name from deserialized or otherwise externally-controlled data, then instantiated with `new`. An attacker who controls that name can point it at any global constructor reachable at runtime, including ones with dangerous side effects in their constructor — Unsafe Reflection (CWE-470, Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code).

Never resolve a class/constructor name from untrusted data against the global namespace. Use an explicit allowlist mapping known-safe names to their constructors instead.

unsafe_reflection_from_deserialized_inpu.benefit: Prevents attacker-controlled data from triggering instantiation of arbitrary, potentially dangerous classes at runtime.

unsafe_require.title: require() with dynamic variable
unsafe_require.risk: require() with a non-literal path allows loading arbitrary modules (CWE-94).

Use only literal paths in require(). Validate inputs if dynamic loading is needed.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unsafe_require.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

unvalidated_dynamic_method_call.title: Global method called by a user-controlled name
unvalidated_dynamic_method_call.risk: Accessing and calling a method on the global object (window, global, process) using a user-controlled property name allows an attacker to call any global function — including eval, require, fetch, or process.exit — enabling code execution or denial of service (CWE-754, CWE-094).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Never use user input to index global objects. Validate the method name against a strict allowlist before invocation.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unvalidated_dynamic_method_call.benefit: Prevents arbitrary global function invocation via user-controlled property access.

url_host_parsing_via_string_split.title: URL host extracted by string split
url_host_parsing_via_string_split.risk: The host/authority is extracted from a URL by splitting the raw string instead of using a real URL parser. Ambiguous inputs (backslashes as authority separators, userinfo tricks like "@", mixed encodings) are interpreted differently by this ad-hoc split than by the browser, proxy, or HTTP client that actually makes the request — an Interpretation Conflict (CWE-436) that can be abused for host confusion / SSRF bypass.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always use the URL API (new URL(input).hostname) instead of manual string splitting to extract host/authority components.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

url_host_parsing_via_string_split.benefit: Ensures host/authority parsing matches the same RFC-compliant logic used by the actual HTTP client, eliminating a class of SSRF and access-control bypasses caused by parser disagreement.

useless_regexp_escape.title: Useless escape in a regex
useless_regexp_escape.risk: A useless backslash escape in a regex string (e.g., \p is just p, \e is just e) may indicate programmer intent to match a special sequence that was silently ignored, leading to a weaker-than-expected pattern and potential security bypass (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Remove useless escapes or use raw string literals (template literals) to avoid inadvertent escape interpretation. Verify each escape sequence is intentional.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

useless_regexp_escape.benefit: Ensures regex patterns match exactly the intended characters without silent escaping bugs.

validate_before_canonicalize.title: Validation before canonicalization
validate_before_canonicalize.risk: A value is checked against an allow/block list, and only afterwards is it decoded or normalized (decodeURIComponent, .normalize(), .toLowerCase()). Validating before canonicalizing means the check runs on a representation of the input that differs from what will actually be used afterwards — an attacker can use an alternate encoding, a homoglyph, or mixed case to slip past the check while still resolving to the blocked value once normalized (CWE-180, Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always canonicalize (decode, normalize, lowercase) the input first, and only then run the allow/block-list check against the canonical form.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

validate_before_canonicalize.benefit: Closes bypasses of allow/block-list checks caused by validating a non-canonical representation of the input.

vue_v_html.title: Vue.js v-html — XSS risk
vue_v_html.risk: v-html directive injects raw HTML without escaping, vulnerable to XSS if content includes user data (CWE-79).

websocket_no_validation.risk: Unvalidated WebSocket messages can contain injection payloads, oversized data, or malformed structures (CWE-20).

Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

websocket_no_validation.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

window_open_noopener.title: window.open without noopener
window_open_noopener.risk: window.open() without rel='noopener' allows the opened page to access window.opener (CWE-1022).

Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

window_open_noopener.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

xpath_injection.title: XPath injection
xpath_injection.risk: Building an XPath expression from user-supplied input allows XPath injection — an attacker can inject XPath operators to bypass authentication (e.g., inject ' or '1'='1 into a credential check), extract arbitrary nodes from the XML document, or cause denial of service (CWE-643).

Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xpath_injection.benefit: Prevents XPath injection enabling authentication bypass and unauthorized XML data extraction.

xss_exception_exposure.title: Exception details sent in the response
xss_exception_exposure.risk: Sending exception messages or stack traces directly to the HTTP response can expose internal implementation details — file paths, library versions, class names — that help attackers develop exploits (CWE-079, CWE-209).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Log the full error server-side and return a generic error message to the client. Never include stack traces or internal paths in production responses.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xss_exception_exposure.benefit: Prevents leakage of internal implementation details via error messages.

xss_jquery_unsafe_plugin.title: jQuery .html() with user input
xss_jquery_unsafe_plugin.risk: jQuery's .html() method with user-controlled input sets innerHTML, executing embedded scripts — equivalent to direct innerHTML assignment and leading to XSS (CWE-079).

Use .text() instead of .html() for plain text content. If HTML is required, sanitize the input with DOMPurify.sanitize() before passing to .html().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xss_jquery_unsafe_plugin.benefit: Prevents XSS via jQuery's .html() method with user-controlled content.

xss_through_dom.title: DOM-based XSS
xss_through_dom.risk: DOM text sourced from browser properties (location.hash, document.referrer, window.name) is reinterpreted as HTML without escaping — an attacker controls these values and can inject arbitrary scripts, achieving DOM-based XSS (CWE-079, CWE-116).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use textContent or innerText instead of innerHTML when inserting plain text. When HTML is required, use DOMPurify.sanitize() before assigning to innerHTML.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xss_through_dom.benefit: Prevents DOM-based XSS via attacker-controlled browser properties.

xss_unsafe_html_construction.title: Unsafe HTML construction
xss_unsafe_html_construction.risk: HTML constructed from user-controlled server input assigned to innerHTML or document.write allows reflected or stored XSS — the browser parses the injected string as HTML, executing embedded scripts (CWE-079, CWE-116).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use textContent for text, or sanitize with DOMPurify.sanitize() before setting innerHTML. On the server side, escape HTML entities before embedding in templates.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

xss_unsafe_html_construction.benefit: Prevents XSS from HTML constructed with user-controlled server data.

db_error_exposed_php.title: DB error exposed in response (PHP)
db_error_exposed_php.risk: A database exception message is echoed directly to the HTTP response. Error output reveals internal details (table names, SQL queries, stack traces) that assist an attacker in mapping the database structure (CWE-209).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Set display_errors=Off in production php.ini. Log exceptions with a framework (Monolog, PSR-3). Return a generic user-facing message instead of the raw exception.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_error_exposed_php.benefit: Prevents information disclosure that enables database schema reconnaissance and targeted injection attacks.

hardcoded_connection_string_php.title: Hardcoded DB credentials (PHP)
hardcoded_connection_string_php.risk: A database connection uses a hardcoded password literal as a direct argument. Credentials in source code appear in version control history, deployment artifacts, and can be extracted by anyone with code access (CWE-798).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Read database password from environment variables: $password = getenv('DB_PASSWORD') or $_ENV['DB_PASSWORD']. Use a .env file loaded by a library like vlucas/phpdotenv, but never commit .env files. Store production secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

hardcoded_connection_string_php.benefit: Prevents database credential exposure via source code and version control history.

idor_missing_ownership_php.title: IDOR: no ownership check (PHP)
idor_missing_ownership_php.risk: A model is loaded directly by an ID taken from the request, with no ownership filter. Changing the ID parameter lets any authenticated user read or modify another user's resource — Insecure Direct Object Reference (CWE-639), the most common API vulnerability.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Always scope the query to the current user, e.g. Order::where('id', $id)->where('user_id', auth()->id())->firstOrFail(), or use Laravel policies/authorize() for object-level access control.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

idor_missing_ownership_php.benefit: Prevents any authenticated user from accessing or tampering with another user's data by guessing or enumerating IDs.

missing_authz_check_admin_controller.title: Admin action without authorization check
missing_authz_check_admin_controller.risk: A controller action performing a sensitive write/administrative operation has no authorization check (can(), authorize(), a Policy, or an admin middleware) — only routing/authentication may protect it, so any authenticated user reaching this action can perform it regardless of their actual role (CWE-862).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Add an explicit authorization check ($this->authorize('update', $model), a Gate::allows() check, or a Policy class) before performing the action.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

missing_authz_check_admin_controller.benefit: Ensures every sensitive controller action enforces role/ownership rules, not just authentication.

naive_domain_suffix_match_php.title: Naive domain suffix match (PHP)
naive_domain_suffix_match_php.risk: A host/cookie domain is matched against an allowed suffix using plain substring/suffix comparison instead of a label-boundary-aware check. "evil-example.com" ends with "example.com" without being a real subdomain, and an IP address can also satisfy a naive suffix check — an attacker can craft a domain that passes the comparison while pointing at infrastructure they control (CWE-346, Origin Validation Error).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Compare domains with an explicit label boundary (a leading "." before the suffix, or parse_url()/a proper public-suffix-aware library), and explicitly reject bare IP addresses where a registrable domain is expected.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

naive_domain_suffix_match_php.benefit: Prevents domain-suffix bypass attacks used to scope cookies or trust to attacker-controlled hosts.

oauth_account_link_without_email_verific.title: OAuth account linked without email verification
oauth_account_link_without_email_verific.risk: A local account is looked up or created by matching the email address returned by an OAuth/OIDC provider, with no check that the provider marked that email as verified. Some identity providers let users self-report an unverified email — an attacker who registers "victim@company.com" as an unverified email at a permissive provider can link to and take over the victim's existing local account (CWE-287, Improper Authentication).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Only link or create an account from an OAuth/OIDC email when the provider's response explicitly marks that email as verified (email_verified: true). Reject or require additional verification otherwise.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

oauth_account_link_without_email_verific.benefit: Prevents account takeover via unverified-email account linking with third-party identity providers.

password_reset_missing_token_binding_php.title: Password reset without token binding
password_reset_missing_token_binding_php.risk: A password is updated with no visible reset-token verification nearby — the target user appears to be selected directly from request data (an ID or email parameter) instead of being derived from a validated, single-use reset token. This lets an attacker reset an arbitrary account's password by supplying its identifier, without ever proving control of that account's email or session — Improper Authorization / Weak Password Recovery Mechanism (CWE-285 / CWE-640).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Never select the target user from request-supplied identifiers for a password reset. Derive the user strictly from a signed, single-use, time-limited reset token (verify it with hash_equals() or a signed-route mechanism) before allowing the update.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

password_reset_missing_token_binding_php.benefit: Prevents account takeover via arbitrary password reset, one of the most severe authentication vulnerability classes.

quadratic_uniqueness_check_in_loop.title: Quadratic uniqueness check in a loop
quadratic_uniqueness_check_in_loop.risk: A uniqueness/membership check (in_array()/array_search()) runs inside a loop over user-controlled data. Each call rescans the whole list, making the operation O(n²) in the number of items — a large or crafted input (many colliding headings, footnotes, or entries) can drive CPU usage disproportionately and cause a denial of service (CWE-407, Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace the linear scan with a hash-map lookup: track seen values as array keys (isset($seen[$value])) instead of calling in_array()/array_search() on a growing list inside the loop.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

quadratic_uniqueness_check_in_loop.benefit: Reduces the operation from O(n²) to O(n), preventing algorithmic-complexity denial of service on large or adversarial input.

sensitive_data_in_redirect.title: Request data sent in a redirect
sensitive_data_in_redirect.risk: A redirect target is built directly from request data and sent as-is in the Location header. If the original request URL still carries sensitive query parameters (tokens, session identifiers), they are forwarded into the redirect and end up in the Referer header sent to whatever host the redirect points to — an unintended disclosure of sensitive information via a trusted channel (CWE-201).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Strip sensitive query parameters before using a value in a redirect, and validate the target against an allowlist of internal paths/hosts rather than forwarding request data verbatim.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sensitive_data_in_redirect.benefit: Prevents session tokens and other sensitive query parameters from leaking to third-party hosts via the Referer header on redirect.

sensitive_field_exposed_response.title: Sensitive model fields in the response
sensitive_field_exposed_response.risk: A user/account model is serialized directly into an HTTP response without filtering out sensitive fields (password hash, API token, secret). Any attribute added to the model later is exposed automatically — CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use an explicit allowlist (->only([...])) or a resource/DTO layer, or mark sensitive attributes as $hidden on the model, instead of serializing the raw model.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

sensitive_field_exposed_response.benefit: Prevents accidental disclosure of credentials and secrets through API responses as the data model evolves.

stored_procedure_dynamic_php.title: Dynamic stored procedure (PHP)

Use PDO prepared statements with named placeholders for all user-supplied values: $stmt = $pdo->prepare("CALL GetUser(:id)"); $stmt->bindParam(':id', $userId). Never concatenate PHP variables into stored procedure calls.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

stored_procedure_dynamic_php.benefit: Eliminates stored procedure injection by enforcing parameterized calls in PHP.

Use escapeshellarg() to sanitize arguments before shell execution.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_cmdi_php.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_open_redirect_php.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_pathtraversal_php.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_sqli_php.risk: An attacker can read, modify, or delete database records.

Use parameterized queries with placeholders (%s, ?).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_sqli_php.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

Encode all user-supplied data before outputting it with htmlspecialchars($val, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') or htmlentities().
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

taint_xss_php.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

unbounded_decompression.title: Decompression without size limit
unbounded_decompression.risk: Compressed input is decompressed with no output-size limit. A crafted archive with a very high compression ratio (a "decompression bomb") can expand to gigabytes from a small payload, exhausting memory and causing a denial of service — CWE-400 / CWE-409.

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Enforce a maximum decompressed size before or during decompression (e.g. pass a length limit to gzinflate(), or decompress incrementally and abort once a size cap is exceeded).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unbounded_decompression.benefit: Prevents memory-exhaustion denial of service from maliciously crafted compressed input.

unrestricted_file_upload_php.title: Unrestricted file upload (PHP)

Validate file type via finfo_file() magic bytes, use pathinfo() to check extension against a strict allowlist, and store files outside the web root with randomized names.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

unrestricted_file_upload_php.benefit: Prevents PHP web shell uploads and arbitrary code execution via unrestricted file upload (CWE-434).

weak_password_hash_php.title: Weak password hashing (PHP)
weak_password_hash_php.risk: Using MD5, SHA1, or SHA256 to hash passwords provides insufficient computational cost — these fast algorithms are crackable in seconds with GPU-based dictionary attacks (CWE-916, OWASP A02).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

weak_password_hash_php.benefit: Ensures password hashes are computationally expensive to crack, making offline brute-force and dictionary attacks impractical (CWE-916).

authenticated_action_missing_authz.title: Authenticated action without authorization check
authenticated_action_missing_authz.risk: A view is protected by @login_required (authentication) but performs a sensitive administrative action with no permission check (authorization). Add an explicit permission check (user.has_perm(...), @staff_member_required, or a DRF permission class) in addition to @login_required for any administrative action.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

authenticated_action_missing_authz.benefit: Ensures administrative actions are restricted to users who actually hold the required role, not merely any logged-in user.

base64_credentials.risk: Base64 is NOT encryption — credentials are readable by simple decoding (CWE-312).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use environment variables or a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

base64_credentials.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

cache_key_missing_user_scope.title: Cache key not scoped to the user
cache_key_missing_user_scope.risk: A response that depends on the requesting user is cached under a fixed/static key (or a key not derived from the user's identity). steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Include the requesting user's identity in the cache key (key_builder that incorporates request.user.id / session id), so cached entries never cross user boundaries.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cache_key_missing_user_scope.benefit: Prevents cross-user data leakage caused by a cache key that does not distinguish between callers.

cache_poisoning.title: Cache Poisoning
cache_poisoning.risk: X-Forwarded-Host and similar headers, if used without validation, allow cache poisoning. A single poisoned response serves malicious content to all users (CWE-444).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate X-Forwarded-Host against ALLOWED_HOSTS. Use Vary headers. Configure CDN to not cache responses with unrecognized headers.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cache_poisoning.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

case_sensitive_blocklist_bypass.title: Case-sensitive allow or block list
case_sensitive_blocklist_bypass.risk: A name (a package name, a header value, a Cache-Control directive) is compared against an allow/block list without first normalizing case. Two values that are logically equivalent but differ only in case (or in header-name case, which HTTP treats as case-insensitive) are treated as different — an attacker can bypass the list simply by changing the case of the value being checked (CWE-178, Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Normalize case (.lower() or .casefold()) on both the value being checked and the entries in the list before comparing, especially for anything HTTP-related (header names/values) which is case-insensitive by specification.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

case_sensitive_blocklist_bypass.benefit: Prevents case-based bypasses of allow/block-list security checks.

cookie_injection.title: Cookie built from user input
cookie_injection.risk: Cookie value built from user-supplied input allows Cookie Poisoning — attacker may inject arbitrary cookie fields or poison shared caches (CWE-020).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Validate and sanitize all user input before including it in a cookie value. Reject values containing special characters (newlines, semicolons, commas).
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cookie_injection.benefit: Prevents cookie poisoning and cache injection attacks.

cors_wildcard_origin.title: CORS allows any origin
cors_wildcard_origin.risk: CORS is configured to accept any origin (allow_origins=["*"]). Any website can then make cross-origin requests to this API from a victim's browser and read the response, since the browser's same-origin protection is explicitly disabled server-side — Origin Validation Error (CWE-346).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Replace the wildcard with an explicit allowlist of trusted origins (allow_origins=["https://app.example.com"]), and never combine a wildcard origin with allow_credentials=True.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

cors_wildcard_origin.benefit: Restores the browser's same-origin protection, preventing arbitrary third-party sites from reading responses from this API on behalf of a logged-in victim.

csrf_missing_flask.title: Missing CSRF protection (Flask)
csrf_missing_flask.risk: Flask POST/PUT/DELETE routes without CSRF protection allow attackers to forge authenticated requests from any website visited by the victim (CWE-352, OWASP A01).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file
Use Flask-WTF (CSRFProtect) for server-rendered forms, or implement SameSite=Strict cookies with token-based authentication for REST APIs.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

csrf_missing_flask.benefit: Prevents cross-site request forgery attacks that could allow unauthorized state-changing actions on behalf of authenticated users (CWE-352).

db_connection_string_credentials.title: DB connection string with credentials (Python)
db_connection_string_credentials.risk: A database connection URL with embedded credentials (protocol://user:password@host/db) stores plaintext credentials in source code. These credentials appear in version control history and can be extracted by anyone with repository access (CWE-522, CWE-798).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Store the connection URL in an environment variable and read it at runtime: DATABASE_URL = os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]. Use a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault) in production. Add .env files to .gitignore.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_connection_string_credentials.benefit: Prevents credential exposure via source code and version control history.

db_error_exposed_python.title: DB error exposed in response (Python)
db_error_exposed_python.risk: A database exception message is returned directly in the HTTP response. Error messages can reveal table names, column names, SQL queries, or stack traces — information that helps an attacker map the database schema (CWE-209).

steps.action: Locate the vulnerable code pattern in the file

Return a generic error message to the client. Log the detailed exception server-side using a logging framework. Use a centralized error handler (Flask errorhandler, Django middleware) to avoid leaking internal details.
Run the audit again to verify the finding is resolved

db_error_exposed_python.benefit: Prevents attackers from using error messages to perform database reconnaissance and plan targeted attacks.

db_superuser_connection_python.title: DB connection as superuser (Python)
